subject: Communication
title: Data Storytelling: Numbers That Move
description: A fast breakdown of Data Storytelling: Numbers That Move for builders.

hook.text: A slide full of charts puts an executive to sleep. One chart with a story behind it gets the budget approved.

buildup.text: Data storytelling combines data, narrative, and visualization to make numbers meaningful and actionable.

discovery.text: The key: don't present data. Present the insight. 'Revenue grew 12%' is data. 'Our new strategy worked' is a story.

twist.text: Most analysts fail because they show all the data. Great data storytellers show only the data that matters.

climax.text: Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic's framework: context (why), data (what happened), narrative (what it means), call to action.

punchline.text: Data informs. Stories from data transform.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between data presentation and data storytelling?
options: Presenting insight and meaning, not just numbers

details.summary: Data storytelling combines data analysis with narrative structure to make numbers meaningful and actionable. Instead of presenting charts, data storytellers frame numbers within a narrative arc: what was happening, what changed, why it matters, and what should be done.
details.whyItMatters: Organizations drown in data but starve for insight. Data storytelling bridges the gap between analysis and action by making numbers emotionally compelling.
takeaways: Frame data within a narrative arc, not just in charts
Context determines whether numbers are meaningful or noise
The best data stories end with a clear call to action

faq.question: What is the difference between data reporting and data storytelling?
faq.answer: Data reporting presents numbers: revenue was 10 million. Data storytelling adds narrative: after three flat quarters, the new strategy drove a 40 percent revenue jump, proving the investment was right. Reporting describes what happened. Storytelling explains why it matters and what to do next.

faq.question: How do you learn to tell stories with data?
faq.answer: Start with the so what question for every data point. Find the human impact behind every number. Structure presentations as problem-insight-action narratives rather than dashboard walkthroughs. Practice turning every chart into a sentence that includes a verb and a consequence.
